pages.title: Extract fields | SwiftAISDK
pages.text:
Extract fields
AI.experimentalExtract
reads one evidence state and returns named extraction answers. OpenAI, Anthropic and Google expose language-backed extraction adapters through their existing structured-generation models. The experimental contract is independent of structured text output and Decision questions.
import
SwiftAI
import
SwiftAIOpenAI
let
provider
=
try
OpenAIProvider
(
configuration
: .
init
(
apiKey
:
"
...
"
))
let
result
=
try
await
AI.
experimentalExtract
(
model
: provider.
extractionModel
(
"
gpt-5.5
"
)
,
state
: .text
(
"
Invoice total: 1200 yen. Issued on 2026-11-14.
"
)
,
fields
: [
"
total
"
:
.
init
(
type
: .
number
,
unit
:
"
JPY
"
,
integer
:
true
)
,
"
issued
"
:
.
init
(
type
: .
date
)
],
referenceDate
:
"
2026-11-14
"
)
let
total
=
result.
answers
[
"
total
"
]
?
.value
Fields support text, number, date, time, datetime, duration and lists of text, number or date items. Field instructions, units, integer/decimal constraints and an optional calendar reference date guide extraction. An absent value is
nil
, with a separate
guess
where the model can supply one. Answers retain confidence,
pNull
, source evidence, usage and provider metadata. Text source offsets count UTF-16 code units. File sources identify the original evidence part.
The facade validates input before model work and checks every returned answer. Unsupported field types, malformed/incomplete answers and refusals throw typed errors for the complete call. Retry settings and abort signals follow native provider conventions. URL evidence uses protected downloads; an explicit
download
function can supply an application-owned downloader.
Use
AIProviderRegistry.extractionModel("provider:model")
for a registered provider. With the compatibility umbrella, the string overload resolves through
AIDefaultProvider
. Its default Gateway provider currently has no extraction factory, so configure a capable provider or pass a model explicitly. ScaleDown is a discovered upstream provider and is not implemented by this release.

pages.text:
deepseek
Package
Section titled “Package”
@ai-sdk/deepseek
Factories
Section titled “Factories”
AIProviders.deepSeek
Capabilities
Section titled “Capabilities”
Language
Files
Current reviewed behavior
Section titled “Current reviewed behavior”
The reviewed baseline is
@ai-sdk/deepseek
3.0.86. The existing
languageModel
/
chatModel
factories retain Chat Completions. Opt into Responses and provider web search explicitly:
let
model
=
provider.
responses
(
"
deepseek-v4-pro
"
)
let
result
=
try
await
model.
generate
(
.
init
(
messages
: [.
user
(
"
Find the latest release notes.
"
)
],
tools
: [
"
search
"
:
DeepSeekTools.
webSearch
()
],
providerOptions
:
DeepSeekResponsesModelOptions
(
reasoningEffort
: .
high
)
.
providerOptions
))
Responses supports structured JSON, image URLs/inline images/provider references, ordered reasoning/tool replay, and unary or incremental SSE results. Reasoning
itemId
, full web-search call/action replay, response IDs, logprobs and exact server-tool usage survive in provider metadata.
thinking: .disabled
sends reasoning effort
none
; portable reasoning maps
medium
to
high
and
xhigh
to
max
, with compatibility warnings.
topLogprobs
and ASCII
userID
are validated before HTTP.
Strict tools, seed, topK, penalties and stop sequences produce unsupported warnings. Image URLs are limited to 8192 UTF-16 units, supported inline formats are JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP, and
fileData
image mode is rejected for Responses. Incomplete/failed/abruptly-ended streams retain their terminal distinction. Model-level behavior is mock-tested; no live-service guarantee is implied.
Current protocol for future model IDs
Section titled “Current protocol for future model IDs”
Unknown model IDs inherit the V4-or-newer protocol, including thinking defaults and required
reasoning_content
on assistant turns. Known
deepseek-chat
,
deepseek-reasoner
and V1–V3 version IDs keep the legacy protocol, including provider-prefixed forms such as
provider/deepseek-v2.5
.
Rotating credentials
Section titled “Rotating credentials”
The native
DeepSeekProviderSettings
accepts an optional
apiKeyProvider
asynchronous throwing closure. It is resolved for each authenticated request, so short-lived credentials can refresh without recreating the provider or model. Static
apiKey
settings remain supported. A supplier failure stops the request before it reaches the transport.
Chat Completions portable reasoning
Section titled “Chat Completions portable reasoning”
Chat Completions portable effort maps to DeepSeek’s
low
,
high
, or
max
settings.
medium
now maps to
low
and
xhigh
to
high
, with compatibility warnings in generation and stream-start metadata. Explicit provider effort retains its existing native option validation and precedence; portable
none
still disables thinking.
Chat Completions tool replay and Azure strict options
Section titled “Chat Completions tool replay and Azure strict options”
Tool arguments retain valid serialized JSON and JSON-quote malformed raw text. Native DeepSeek Chat Completions strict tools still require the beta endpoint and consistent strict mode. Azure-hosted configurations have unknown strict-tool capability; they forward each tool’s explicit true/false/omitted choice without applying the native beta-only policy.
Notes
Section titled “Notes”
DeepSeek chat models mirror upstream DeepSeek 3.0.86:
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
, custom base URL and headers, callable/language/chat aliases,
deepseek.chat
provider IDs, versioned user-agent suffix, reasoning/thinking mapping, providerOptions.deepseek thinking and reasoningEffort schema, cache-aware usage/provider metadata, JSON response instruction injection, generated fallback IDs for missing generate tool-call IDs, streaming response metadata, stream usage, OpenAI-compatible tool calls including strict mode, DeepSeek V4 assistant reasoning_content rules, V4 Flash Vision Exp inline, URL, and provider-reference images, Files V4 upload with
user_data
, expiry validation and structured errors, and unsupported embedding/image-generation families. The 3.0.37 pass also covered model-aware reasoning/sampling rules, log probabilities, user/message metadata, strict function-tool preparation, upload preflight and response metadata, complete usage, and typed stream failures. ProviderV4 type names, ESM-only packaging, Node 22 engines, and workflow serialization helpers are JS-only upstream concerns. The 2026-09-20 pass aligns empty-choice failures with the exact upstream structural error. The 2026-09-27 pass preserves multimodal V4 and Flash tool-result text, provider references, URL and base64 images, and rejects unsupported image URL media types. Standard cached prompt-token details are used when provider-specific cache-hit counts are absent. The 2026-10-11 pass: Common xhigh and max reasoning both map to max; native file bytes already cover the published Blob type-only cleanup. The 2026-10-18 pass: Future DeepSeek models use the V4 protocol unless recognized as legacy chat/reasoner/R1/V3 identifiers. The 2026-11-01 reviewed delta adds native per-request async credentials and current portable request/stream fixes where applicable; see WeeklyUpstreamAudit20261101 for exact package dispositions and retained gaps. The 2026-11-08 reviewed delta and retained gaps are documented in WeeklyUpstreamAudit20261108; no full-package or live-service parity is implied. The 2026-11-14 reviewed delta and retained gaps are documented in WeeklyUpstreamAudit20261114; no full-package or live-service parity is implied.

minimax
Package
Section titled “Package”
@ai-sdk/minimax
Factories
Section titled “Factories”
AIProviders.miniMax
Capabilities
Section titled “Capabilities”
Language
Image
Video
Current reviewed behavior
Section titled “Current reviewed behavior”
The reviewed baseline is
@ai-sdk/minimax
3.0.81.
image("MiniMax-H3-Image")
and
imageModel("MiniMax-H3-Image-Highspeed")
now support text-to-image and reference-image editing.
MiniMaxProviderSettings.imageBaseURL
defaults to
https://api.minimax.io/v1
; the existing settings initializer selector remains available.
let
image
=
try
await
provider.image(
"
MiniMax-H3-Image
"
).
generateImage
(
.
init
(
prompt
:
"
A red circle
"
,
aspectRatio
:
"
1:1
"
,
count
:
2
,
providerOptions
:
MiniMaxImageModelOptions
(
area
: .
twoK
,
outputFormat
: .
png
)
.
providerOptions
))
Requests use
/images/generations
or
/images/edits
, always request URL output and securely download successful images through the configured transport. Bearer tokens and provider headers are omitted from downloads. Results contain normalized base64 images, per-image size/revised prompt, output format/request ID and usage details (request usage appears once in per-image metadata).
The maximum advertised batch size is ten. Individual image failures become warnings while successful images survive; seed is unsupported, masks fail before HTTP, and edits warn and omit the generation-only prompt-enhancement option. Compression accepts integers from 0 through 100. Async credentials continue to resolve only for authenticated provider requests.
M3.1 reasoning and sampling
Section titled “M3.1 reasoning and sampling”
minimax-m3.1-flash
and later M-series versions support explicit reasoning effort, image/video input, and MiniMax cache markers. Model IDs are compared by numeric version components: M3.10 and M4 inherit these capabilities. M3.0, older models, and unrecognized IDs retain the earlier Anthropic-compatible behavior.
Set
reasoning
to
low
,
medium
,
high
,
xhigh
, or
max
, or pass
MiniMaxLanguageModelOptions(effort: .high).providerOptions
.
minimal
maps to low effort with a compatibility warning.
none
also maps to low effort with a warning because these models always reason. Explicit
minimax.effort
or
anthropic.effort
takes precedence. Omit reasoning or use
provider-default
to retain the server default.
When reasoning is mapped to MiniMax effort, usage metadata is available under both
anthropic
and
minimax
in generation results and stream finish metadata.
M3.1 and later accept temperature from 0 through 2. Temperature and top-p remain available with adaptive thinking; top-k is removed with a warning. Earlier models retain the Anthropic temperature and thinking restrictions.
Images and video in chat
Section titled “Images and video in chat”
Use image URLs, inline
.data
/
.file
content,
.videoURL(...)
, or a video reference returned by MiniMax. Hosted image and video URLs pass through to the provider. Uploaded video IDs use the
minimax
reference key; the adapter adds
mm_file://
once. Image file references are unsupported.
let
provider
=
try
AIProviders.
miniMax
()
let
model
=
try
provider.
languageModel
(
"
minimax-m3.1-flash
"
)
let
request
=
LanguageModelRequest
(
messages
: [
AIMessage
(
role
: .
user
,
content
: [
.text
(
"
Describe what changes between these scenes.
"
)
,
.
imageURL
(
"
https://example.com/scene.png
"
,
providerMetadata
:
MiniMaxImagePartOptions
(
detail
: .
high
)
.
providerOptions
)
,
.
videoURL
(
"
https://example.com/clip.mp4
"
,
providerMetadata
:
MiniMaxVideoPartOptions
(
fps
:
1
)
.
providerOptions
)
,
.
providerReference
(
mimeType
:
"
video/mp4
"
,
reference
: [
"
minimax
"
:
"
uploaded-video-id
"
]
)
]
)
],
reasoning
:
"
high
"
)
let
result
=
try
await
model.
generate
(
request
)
print
(
result.text
)
Image detail supports
low
,
default
, or
high
. Video fps must be a finite number from 0.2 through 5. Omitted options use server defaults; invalid values fail before the request is sent. PDF input continues through the shared Anthropic document conversion. The same media and reasoning options work with
stream
.
Prompt caching
Section titled “Prompt caching”
Attach
MiniMaxCacheControlOptions(cacheControl: .ephemeral).providerOptions
as message or content-part
providerMetadata
. A message marker applies to its final block unless that block already has its own marker. The
minimax
namespace takes precedence over the canonical
anthropic
namespace; both
cacheControl
and
cache_control
spellings work. Up to four breakpoints are retained across prompt blocks and tools, with a warning for each excess marker. A marker does not guarantee a cache hit.
Video generation
Section titled “Video generation”
videoModel(...)
continues to support async video operations and polling independently of chat video input. Persist the returned operation to resume status checks. Polling treats the task ID as one URL path segment, including IDs containing slashes or standalone dots. Chat file references require an existing uploaded MiniMax file; this provider does not add a file-upload client.
Refreshable credentials and portable reasoning
Section titled “Refreshable credentials and portable reasoning”
MiniMaxProviderSettings.apiKeyProvider
accepts an asynchronous throwing closure and refreshes credentials before each Messages or video HTTP request. Model construction does not call it; supplier errors propagate before sending. Existing static keys and custom-header precedence remain supported.
On M3.1 and later, portable
none
and
minimal
reasoning select
low
effort with the shared compatibility warning. Explicit provider effort still takes precedence. The native open-string API continues to warn and omit invalid reasoning strings, which are outside upstream’s typed reasoning union.
Admission tiers
Section titled “Admission tiers”
MiniMaxLanguageModelOptions(serviceTier: .priority)
requests priority admission;
.standard
requests standard admission. Both map to
service_tier
for unary and streaming Messages. Omit the field for the provider default. The
minimax
namespace overrides
anthropic
; known foreign tiers warn and are omitted, while invalid or null tier values fail before I/O.
Notes
Section titled “Notes”
MiniMax language and video models mirror upstream 3.0.81:
MINIMAX_API_KEY
, separate language/video base URLs, custom headers, versioned user-agent suffix, callable provider plus
languageModel
/
chat
and
video
/
videoModel
aliases, and
minimax.messages
/
minimax.video
provider IDs. Language reuses the Anthropic Messages request builder, error handling, streaming lifecycle, telemetry metadata, and ordered generate-content parser, including signed/redacted reasoning, citation metadata, compaction, and adaptive/disabled thinking options. MiniMax H3/H3-Max video uses model-aware 480P/768P/2K tiers, duration bounds, audio support, and reference-input validation, and covers text-to-video, first/last-frame and reference-to-video inputs, 2K resolution and ratio mapping, reference audio, text-to-video
16:9
default/fallback behavior, duration/cap warnings, submit/poll lifecycle, aborts, structured errors, response/provider metadata, and custom polling controls. Embedding remains unsupported. Status polling now follows only validated redirects and never forwards credentials away from the configured origin. The 2026-10-23 pass: M3.1+ and future model IDs support image/video inputs and reasoning effort; older M2 families remain text-only. MiniMax cache options and sampling semantics use the compatible Messages hooks. The 2026-11-01 reviewed delta adds native per-request async credentials and current portable request/stream fixes where applicable; see WeeklyUpstreamAudit20261101 for exact package dispositions and retained gaps. The 2026-11-08 reviewed delta and retained gaps are documented in WeeklyUpstreamAudit20261108; no full-package or live-service parity is implied. The 2026-11-14 reviewed delta and retained gaps are documented in WeeklyUpstreamAudit20261114; no full-package or live-service parity is implied.
